questions.stem: Why can gases be compressed but liquids cannot?

options.text: Gas particles are smaller than liquid particles
Gas particles are far apart with lots of empty space, while liquid particles are already close together
Gas particles have weaker bonds than liquid particles
Liquid particles are heavier than gas particles

questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with lots of empty space between them. When pressure is applied, the particles can be pushed closer together, reducing the volume. In liquids, particles are already close together with very little space between them, so they cannot be compressed further.

questions.stem: How do particles move in a solid?

options.text: They do not move at all
They move freely around each other
They move quickly in all directions

questions.explanation: In a solid, particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces between them. They vibrate about these fixed positions but do not move to new positions. This is why solids have a fixed shape and volume. It is a common mistake to say particles in a solid do not move - they do vibrate.
